{{nihongo|'''Kukuhi Shrine'''|久久比神社}} is a [[shinto shrine]] in the [[Engishiki Jinmyōchō]]. It is located in [[Tajima Province]].

'''Kukuhi Shrine''' (くくひじんじゃ) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|abstract|Q845945|ar|جينجا|arz|ضريح شنتو|bcl|Shinto shrine|ca|Jinja|cs|Šintoistická svatyně|da|Shinto-tempel|de|Shintō-Schrein|el|Σιντοϊστικό Ιερό|eo|Ŝintoa sanktejo|es|Jinja|eu|Jinja|fa|معبد شینتویی|fi|Šintolainen pyhäkkö|fr|Sanctuaire shinto|hi|शिंतो मंदिर|hr|Šintoistički hram|hu|Sintó szentély|id|Jinja|it|Jinja|ja|神社|ka|ძინძია|ko|신사 (신토)|lb|Shintō-Schräin|mr|शिंतो मंदिर|nl|Jinja (heiligdom)|no|Jinja|or|ଜିଞ୍ଜା|pl|Jinja|pt|Templo xintoísta|ru|Дзиндзя|sc|Jinja|simple|Shinto shrine|sl|Šintoistično svetišče|sr|Шинтоистички храм|sv|Jinja|th|ศาลเจ้าชินโต|tok|tomo sewi pi nasin sewi Sinto|tr|Şinto tapınağı|uk|Святилище (синто)|uz|Dzindzya|vi|Thần xã|wuu|神社|zh|神社|zh_yue|神社|qid=Q845945}} in Shimonomiya, {{ill|Toyooka, Hyōgo|Q696388|qid=Q696388}}, {{ill|Hyōgo Prefecture|Q130290|qid=Q130290}}. It is a {{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|abstract|Q11064932|fr|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|ja|延喜式神名帳|simple|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|zh|延喜式神名帳|qid=Q11064932|lt=Shikinai small shrine}}, and its former rank under the {{ill|Q712534|lt=shrine ranking system}} was village shrine.

=== Enshrined deity ===
* {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Kukunochi-no-Kami}} (くくのちのかみ)

=== History ===
The {{ill|Honden|Q2044994|qid=Q2044994}} is a three-bay nagare-zukuri structure with a kokera-buki roof. It was built in {{ill|Eishō (Muromachi period)|Q1193577|qid=Q1193577}} 4 ({{ill|1507|ab|1507|af|1507|als|1507|am|1507 እ.ኤ.አ.|an|1507|ar|1507|ary|1507|arz|1507|ast|1507|avk|1507|az|1507|azb|۱۵۰۷ (میلادی)|bcl|1507|be|1507|be_x_old|1507|bg|1507|bn|১৫০৭|bpy|মারি ১৫০৭|br|1507|bs|1507.|ca|1507|cdo|1507 nièng|ceb|1507|ckb|١٥٠٧|crh|1507|cs|1507|cv|1507|cy|1507|da|1507|de|1507|diq|1507|el|1507|eml|1507|eo|1507|es|1507|et|1507|eu|1507|fa|۱۵۰۷ (میلادی)|fi|1507|fo|1507|fr|1507|frr|1507|fur|1507|fy|1507|ga|1507|gan|1507年|gcr|1507|gd|1507|gl|1507|he|1507|hi|१५०७|hr|1507.|ht|1507 (almanak jilyen)|hu|1507|hy|1507|ia|1507|id|1507|ilo|1507|io|1507|is|1507|it|1507|ja|1507年|jv|1507|ka|1507|kaa|1507|kk|1507 жыл|ko|1507년|krc|1507 джыл|la|1507|lb|1507|li|1507|lij|1507|lmo|1507|lt|1507 m.|lv|1507. gads|mai|१५०७|map_bms|1507|mdf|1507|mg|1507|mhr|1507|mi|1507|min|1507|mk|1507|mr|इ.स. १५०७|mrj|1507 и|ms|1507|my|၁၅၀၇|mzn|۱۵۰۷|nah|1507|nap|1507|nds|1507|new|सन् १५०७|nl|1507|nn|1507|no|1507|nrm|1507|nso|1507|oc|1507|or|୧୫୦୭|os|1507-æм аз|pa|1507|pl|1507|pnb|1507|pt|1507|qu|1507|ro|1507|ru|1507 год|rue|1507|sa|१५०७|sah|1507|scn|1507|sd|1507ع|se|1507|sh|1507.|shn|1507|simple|1507|sk|1507|sl|1507|smn|1507|sq|1507|sr|1507|su|1507|sv|1507|sw|1507|ta|1507|tg|Соли 1507|th|พ.ศ. 2050|tk|1507|tl|1507|tly|1507|tr|1507|tt|1507 ел|uk|1507|ur|1507ء|uz|1507|vec|1507|vi|1507|vls|1507|wa|1507|war|1507|wuu|1507年|xmf|1507|yi|1507|zh|1507年|zh_min_nan|1507 nî|zh_yue|1507年|qid=Q6161}}) in the {{ill|Muromachi period|Q334845|qid=Q334845}}, and is designated a national {{ill|Important Cultural Property (Japan)|Q1188622|qid=Q1188622}}. Edo-period records describe it as an old shrine also called Munakata Daimyōjin, and there is also a theory that it enshrined {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Tagiribime-no-Mikoto}}.

=== Stork legend ===
According to the {{ill|Nihon Shoki|ar|نيهون شوكي|as|নিহন শ্ব'কি|az|Nihon şoki|bcl|Nihon Shoki|bg|Нихоншоки|ca|Nihon Shoki|cs|Nihonšoki|de|Nihonshoki|el|Νιχόν Σόκι|eo|Nihon Ŝoki|es|Nihonshoki|eu|Nihon Shoki|fa|نیهون شوکی|fi|Nihonshoki|fr|Nihon shoki|gl|Nihon Shoki|he|ניהון שוקי|hi|निहोन शोकी|hr|Nihon Shoki|hu|Nihonsoki|id|Nihon Shoki|it|Nihon shoki|ja|日本書紀|jv|Nihon Shoki|ko|일본서기|la|Nihon Shoki|mk|Нихон шоки|ms|Nihon Shoki|my|နိဟွန်းရှောခိ|nl|Nihon Shoki|no|Nihonshoki|oc|Nihon shoki|pl|Nihon-shoki|pt|Nihon Shoki|rsk|Нихон Шоки|ru|Нихон сёки|sco|Nihon Shoki|sh|Nihon Shoki|simple|Nihon Shoki|sl|Nihon Šoki|sq|Nihon Shoki|sr|Нихон шоки|sv|Nihonshoki|ta|நிஹான் ஷோகி|th|นิฮงโชกิ|tl|Nihon Shoki|tr|Nihon Shoki|uk|Ніхон Сьокі|uz|Nihon shoki|vi|Nhật Bản thư kỷ|zh|日本書紀|zh_min_nan|Ji̍t-pún Su-kì|zh_yue|日本書紀|qid=Q813935}}, on the first day of the tenth month in the 23rd year of Emperor {{ill|Emperor Suinin|Q314850|qid=Q314850}}, while the emperor stood before the palace with Prince '''Homutsuwake''' (誉津別皇子), a '''kugui''' (an old word for {{ill|Oriental stork|ar|لقلق أبيض شرقي|arz|لقلق ابيض شرقى|bg|Черноклюн щъркел|bh|सिकोनिया बॉयसियाना|bn|উদয়ী মানিকজোড়|br|C'hwibon ar reter|ca|Cigonya oriental|ceb|Ciconia boyciana|cs|Čáp východní|cy|Ciconia gwyn y Dwyrain|da|Manchurerstork|de|Schwarzschnabelstorch|eo|Orienta cikonio|es|Ciconia boyciana|et|Ida-toonekurg|eu|Zikoina mokobeltz|fa|لک‌لک خاوری|fr|Cigogne orientale|fy|Swartsnaffelearrebarre|he|חסידה מזרחית|hu|Feketecsőrű gólya|hy|Հեռավորարևելյան արագիլ|it|Ciconia boyciana|ja|コウノトリ|ko|황새|lt|Kininis gandras|mn|Дорнын өрөвтас|nl|Zwartsnavelooievaar|nv|Náátsʼózídę́ę́ʼ tsídii bidaanézí|pl|Bocian czarnodzioby|pnb|اوریانٹل سٹارک|pt|Cegonha-oriental|ro|Barză orientală|ru|Дальневосточный аист|sah|Үрүҥ эһир|sk|Bocian čiernozobý|sv|Amurstork|tr|Ciconia boyciana|uk|Лелека далекосхідний|vi|Hạc trắng Á Đông|war|Ciconia boyciana|zh|东方白鹳|qid=Q998495}}) cried as it crossed the sky.
When the prince asked, "What is that?", the emperor rejoiced greatly and asked his retainers who could capture the bird.
'''{{ill|Ame-no-Yukawata|ja|天湯河板挙|qid=Q52319907}}''' said, "I will surely capture and present it," and pursued the great bird through many provinces; it is said he captured it in {{ill|Izumo Province|ar|إزومو (مقاطعة)|ca|Província d'Izumo|cs|Provincie Izumo|de|Provinz Izumo|es|Provincia de Izumo|fa|ولایت ایزومو|fr|Province d'Izumo|gl|Provincia de Izumo|id|Provinsi Izumo|it|Izumo (provincia)|ja|出雲国|ka|იზუმოს პროვინცია|ko|이즈모국|lt|Idzumo žemė|nl|Izumo (provincie)|no|Izumo|pt|Província de Izumo|ru|Идзумо (провинция)|simple|Izumo Province|sk|Izumo (provincia)|sr|Провинција Изумо|tr|Izumo (vilayet)|uk|Провінція Ідзумо|wuu|出云国|zh|出雲國|zh_classical|出雲國|zh_min_nan|Izumo-kok|zh_yue|出雲國|qid=Q582846}}, or according to another tradition, in {{ill|Tajima Province|Q1053727|qid=Q1053727}}.
On the first day of the eleventh month, he successfully presented the bird. At that time the prince was thirty years old, but had still not spoken and only made sounds like a crying child; on that day he spoke human words for the first time.
Because the kugui was such a sacred bird, its nesting place was called Kukuhi. Later, a shrine was built there and the tree deity '''Kukunochi-no-Kami''' was enshrined.
This is said to be the beginning of Kukuhi Shrine.

At that time, however, the '''Toyooka Basin''' was called "Kimesaki no Umi" and was entirely an inlet of the sea; Shimonomiya stood on the shoreline of that inlet.
The area was also densely wooded, a place where {{ill|Kodama (spirit)|ar|كوداما|as|কোডামা|de|Kodama (Geist)|es|Kodama|fi|Kodama|fr|Kodama|ga|Kodama (sprid)|id|Kodama (mitologi)|it|Kodama (mitologia)|ja|木霊|ko|고다마|mk|Кодама (дух)|mni|ꯀꯣꯗꯃ (ꯊꯋꯥꯢ)|no|Kodama|pl|Kodama (duch)|pt|Kodama|ro|Kodama (spirit)|ru|Кодама|th|โคดามะ|tr|Kodama|uk|Кодама (дух)|zh|木靈|qid=Q1515938}} were thought to dwell, and a scenic site where kami themselves were believed to reside.
It is therefore natural that earlier people perceived the mystery and sacredness of this nature, worshipped the tree deity Kukunochi-no-Kami, and revered the great divine virtue of trees.

=== Amulets ===
Amulets designed with storks (red, green, and purple) are well known as charms for fertility and safe childbirth (based on the tradition that storks bring children). In the fallow season (mainly September to May), storks fly in to the adjacent wetland.
